- Or simpler: create a list of `int[]` pairs `{b[i], a[i]}` and sort by first element descending.
- The C# code sorts `b` (keys) and `a` (items) ascending. Then iterates from `m-1` down to 0 (descending order of b).
- So in Java, sort pairs by `b` ascending, iterate backwards. Or sort descending and iterate forwards.

source_data.prob_desc_description: A burglar got into a matches warehouse and wants to steal as many matches as possible. In the warehouse there are m containers, in the i-th container there are ai matchboxes, and each matchbox contains bi matches. All the matchboxes are of the same size. The burglar's rucksack can hold n matchboxes exactly. Your task is to find out the maximum amount of matches that a burglar can carry away. He has no time to rearrange matches in the matchboxes, that's why he just chooses not more than n matchboxes so that the total amount of matches in them is maximal.
source_data.prob_desc_output_spec: Output the only number — answer to the problem.
source_data.prob_desc_input_spec: The first line of the input contains integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·108) and integer m (1 ≤ m ≤ 20). The i + 1-th line contains a pair of numbers ai and bi (1 ≤ ai ≤ 108, 1 ≤ bi ≤ 10). All the input numbers are integer.
